citations.claim: At step 10 body 0 overlaps wall 0 by 0.388 (distance_to_surface -0.388), violating the 0.15 limit
One step earlier at step 9 the body was still clear of the wall (distance +0.268), so penetration occurred on the final step
At step 8 body was further clear (distance +0.926), showing fast leftward approach at vx ~ -40.9 into thin 0.1-wide wall

counterfactual.change: Reduced horizontal speed from vx=-40.89 to vx=-10 (one field), keeping all else identical; fast approach into thin wall no longer produces deep overlap.

explanation: High-speed (vx~-40.9, ~0.64 units/step) large-radius (r~1.19) body strikes a minimum-thickness (0.1) vertical wall. Despite ~22 substeps per step (~0.03 travel per substep), contact/positional correction fails to stop the body: it goes from clear (+0.27 at step 9) to deeply embedded (-0.39 at step 10, overlap 0.388 > 0.15 limit). Likely impulse plus positional correction is insufficient for thin-wall, high-momentum impact, allowing deep penetration in one step. Slowing vx to -10 removes the failure.
vision_note: The red circle moves leftward toward the thin vertical wall from steps 7 to 9 while remaining clear of it. At step 10 it reaches the bottom of the wall and visibly overlaps and embeds into the wall instead of stopping or bouncing.
